places.rationale: Steady growth from a low base makes 'better' the default; the tail risks are extreme heat, groundwater depletion and war with Pakistan. Superintelligence threatens the IT-services export model but cheapens medicine and energy.

reading.reason: Cheaper goods and wide diffusion help a poor, AI-literate population, but IT and outsourcing exports are what AI replaces first.

places.rationale: Consumption is still a third of rich-world levels with room to grow, but a shrinking, ageing population and a Taiwan or US conflict are the main ways it stalls. As one of two AI powers it gains most from superintelligence if it avoids war.

reading.reason: China owns compute, models and robot factories, so it captures AI rents; the drag is power concentration and an arms race with the US.

places.rationale: Rich, energy-exporting and the AI leader, so abundance is plausible only with superintelligence, which still needs a ninefold rise to lift nine in ten residents. Polarisation, debt and a great-power war are the main downside risks.

reading.reason: The US owns most frontier compute and models, so ownership and productivity dominate; white-collar job losses and polarisation drag.

places.rationale: A stable, growing middle-income economy with energy and mineral exports; very poor safe-water access, a sinking capital and coal dependence are the vulnerabilities.

reading.reason: A large domestic market and nickel for batteries keep it relevant; cheaper goods and medicine outweigh modest export job losses.

places.rationale: Political instability, extreme water stress on the Indus, fast population growth and nuclear rivalry with India give it one of the highest collapse risks here. Growth from a low base still makes 'better' most likely.

reading.reason: Textile exports and Gulf remittances are exposed and a fragile military-led state gains surveillance power; cheaper goods only partly offset.

places.rationale: Consumption per person has stalled for a decade while the population heads toward half a billion; insecurity, weak governance and declining oil rents keep stagnation and collapse risks high.

reading.reason: Cheap medicine, solar and AI services help a poor, young population most, but falling oil rents and a weak state limit the gains.

places.rationale: Food, energy and mineral wealth make 'better' likely, but slow growth, high inequality, crime and drought risk to farming and the Amazon keep stagnation sizeable; inequality also makes abundance for nine in ten hard.

reading.reason: Fairly high AI use helps and a commodity exporter loses few jobs to AI, but deep inequality and crime limit how widely gains spread.

places.rationale: Strong past gains in health and income, but the most climate-exposed delta here faces sea-level rise, cyclones and heat, and its growth model rests on low-wage garment exports.

reading.reason: Garment exports and remittances are routine labour that robots replace, and AI use is very low; cheaper goods only partly offset the loss.

places.rationale: A petrostate at war with a shrinking population faces falling fossil-fuel rents as the world decarbonises, so stagnation is a real possibility, and it is a principal party to nuclear risk.

reading.reason: Cheaper energy erodes its oil and gas rents, sanctions limit AI access, and an authoritarian state at war uses AI for control.

places.rationale: Fast growth from a very low base makes 'better' likely, but recurrent civil war, drought and famine risk and a weak state keep collapse odds high.

reading.reason: Very poor households gain most from cheap medicine, energy and farming advice; little AI access and a fragile state limit the rest.

places.rationale: Tied to the US economy with decent AI uptake, but slow growth, cartel violence, high inequality and severe water stress in the centre and north cap its outlook.

reading.reason: US proximity spreads AI gains, but export assembly and remittances from US jobs are exposed, and cartels can exploit new tools.

places.rationale: Decades of near-flat consumption, the world's oldest population, huge public debt and 87% energy imports make stagnation likely without superintelligence; a strong state and robotics make it a big winner with it.

reading.reason: Robots and AI fill an ageing workforce's gaps and cheaper energy eases import dependence; it owns robotics but not frontier models.

places.rationale: Extreme water stress on the Nile, heavy food imports, a fast-growing population and a debt-burdened state make decline and collapse risks among the highest here.

reading.reason: Cheap energy for desalination and cheaper food imports matter most to a Nile-dependent state; authoritarian control limits the rest.

places.rationale: Solid growth and a young population favour 'better', but typhoons, sea-level rise and a South China Sea flashpoint are risks, and its export model is services labour.

reading.reason: Call-centre outsourcing and overseas workers' remittances are exactly the labour AI and robots replace, despite fairly high AI use.

places.rationale: One of the poorest and least governed countries, with war in the east, 40% undernourished and under a quarter with electricity; its mineral wealth has historically fuelled conflict rather than consumption.

reading.reason: Cheap medicine and solar help the very poor, but AI-era demand for its cobalt and copper may feed conflict more than households.

places.rationale: A capable, stable state with strong growth makes 'better' very likely; the Mekong delta's exposure to sea-level rise and reliance on export assembly are the main risks.

reading.reason: High AI uptake and a capable state help, but its electronics-assembly export model is the routine manufacturing robots replace.

places.rationale: A water crisis that threatens Tehran, sanctions, a repressive and unstable regime and war with Israel and the US make decline or collapse unusually likely for a middle-income country.

reading.reason: Sanctions cut its AI access and cheap energy cuts oil rents, while a repressive state in conflict with Israel and the US gains surveillance.

places.rationale: A fairly rich industrial economy with strong long-run growth, held back by chronic inflation, autocratic drift, earthquake risk and a volatile neighbourhood.

reading.reason: Cheaper energy helps a country importing 70% of its energy, but textile and car-assembly exports are exposed to automation.

places.rationale: Rich, egalitarian and well governed, so 'better' is the base case, but energy imports, ageing and industrial erosion make stagnation plausible without superintelligence.

reading.reason: High AI use and a strong state spread gains widely; it imports frontier models, and its engineering exports face AI and Chinese rivals.

places.rationale: An upper-middle-income economy ageing before it is rich, with slow growth, recurring coups, water stress and flood-prone Bangkok; 'better' is still likely over 75 years.

reading.reason: Robots offset a fast-ageing workforce and tourism resists automation, but car-assembly exports are exposed and coups recur.
